state: Finite byte strings s and query q; count observation is u128; allocations must succeed.
forward: contains(q) iff q is a contiguous substring of s, including empty. distinct_substrings is the cardinality of the set of nonempty substrings.
inverse: Universe is (s,q,b,count). Exclude b disagreeing with interval occurrence (empty occurs), and counts unequal to the cardinality of nonempty interval values. State numbering and occurrence multiplicities are not observable.

For a complete membership language L, compatible texts are exactly s with substring-set including empty equal to L. A realizable finite L has a unique longest word s, recovering the text. Count alone admits all texts with that count: ab and ba both give 3; a count does not recover symbols.
cost: For n bytes and alphabet size sigma<=256, O(n log sigma) construction plus O(n sigma) clone-map copying (O(n) for fixed byte alphabet), O(n sigma) conservative storage. Query O(|q| log sigma), count O(n). No timings measured.
checks: Compiled semantic mutant rejected by a real assertion; syntax generated twice.
limitations: Partial syntax, finite evidence, no timing or downstream gain claimed.
